title: Multi-Agent System Reasoning on Blockchain Networks
summary: Proposes a novel consensus mechanism for LLM-driven agent swarms operating on-chain. Introduces Byzantine fault tolerance adapted for non-deterministic AI outputs. Tested across 1,000 agent simulations with 99.2% agreement rate.

title: Decentralized GPU Routing for Autonomous Agents
summary: Addresses the compute allocation problem in decentralized agent networks. Proposes a market-based routing protocol where agents bid for GPU resources using on-chain micropayments. Benchmarked on Bittensor subnet architecture.

title: Constitutional Governance in Personal AI Operating Systems
summary: Framework for embedding governance rules into personal AI agents. Agents operate within constitutional boundaries set by the user, with on-chain audit trails. Implications for L4+ autonomous systems.

title: Token Incentive Alignment in Multi-Agent Economies
summary: Examines how token-based incentive mechanisms affect cooperation in agent swarms. Finds that poorly designed tokenomics lead to adversarial emergent behavior in 34% of tested scenarios.

title: Persistent Memory Architectures for Long-Running LLM Agents
summary: Compares five approaches to agent memory persistence: vector stores, graph databases, key-value caches, file-based logs, and hybrid architectures. Finds that hybrid approaches outperform single-method by 2.3x on 30-day retention benchmarks.
